title_he: אַהֲבַת אֱלֹהִים גָּבְהָה, לֹא מְדָדָהּ שֵׂכֶל עָרוּם
review: 1:1–1:4 אוֹדֶה לְמִי שֶׁאֲהֵבַנִי … בְּדַם הַיָּדִיד — Rev 1:5 (לָנוּ אוֹהֵב … וַיִּרְחָץ אוֹתָנוּ מִדָּמוֹ); the Arabic أَشْكُرُ مَنْ أَحَبَّنِي … دَمُ ذَاكَ الْحَبِيب is that thanksgiving, and the Hebrew keeps the washing-to-cleansing verb רָחַץ.

2:1–2:2 אַהֲבַת אֵל נִשְׂגָּבָה … שֵׂכֶל עָרוּם — the Arabic مَا قَاسَهَا عَقْلٌ فَطِين is 'no shrewd mind measured it', echoing Eph 3:19 (אַהֲבַת הַמָּשִׁיחַ אֲשֶׁר לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל־דַּעַת); the Hebrew keeps שֵׂכֶל and the participle עָרוּם ('shrewd', as in Gen 3:1) rather than the Modern חָכָם.

3:1–3:4 is the 'sea of ink' motif (if every sea were ink, every sky paper, every grass a pen); the Arabic لَوْ صَارَ حِبْرًا كُلُّ يَمّ … وَالْكُلُّ فِي النَّسْخِ اشْتَرَك — the Hebrew keeps the four instruments and the copying verb יַעְתִּיקוּ, and its nearest scriptural anchor is John 21:25 (לֹא יַסְפִּיקוּ הַסְּפָרִים לִכְתֹּב), which the stanza then applies to Christ's love.

3:7 גָּבְהָה רָמָה שָׁטְפָה גָּאֲתָה — the Arabic فَاقَتْ سَمَتْ فَاضَتْ طَمَتْ is four rising verbs with no object; the Hebrew keeps four verbs (soared, rose, overflowed, surged) so the line reads as the swell it describes, not as a definition.

2:7 מַנְחֵם וּפוֹדֵם — 'guiding and ransoming them'; the Arabic يَهْدِيهُمُ يَفْدِيهُمُ is that pair, and the Hebrew keeps both participles with the pronominal suffix, so the double action of the stanza stays on the perishing (2:4) as its object.
